structured_output.hypothesis: Among sunflower seedheads, the Fibonacci parastichy pair counted increases with head size (diameter), so that small heads show lower pairs and the largest heads show higher pairs such as 55/89 or 89/144, within the same species (Helianthus annuus).
structured_output.pass_criterion: Among heads with a clean Fibonacci parastichy pair and a recorded head diameter, the Spearman correlation between head diameter and the larger parastichy number is positive with rho >= 0.5 (p < 0.01), AND at least three distinct consecutive Fibonacci pairs (e.g. 21/34, 34/55, 55/89) are each observed in at least 5 heads, with median diameter rising monotonically across the pairs.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Spearman rho < 0.2 or not significant at p < 0.01, OR fewer than three distinct Fibonacci pairs each represented by at least 5 heads, OR median diameter does not increase monotonically across pairs. If the dataset has no head-size field usable for the test, the test is undecidable and the claim stays untested.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's 'entire structure varies greatly in size' maps to the diameter of the sunflower head (capitulum); his 'arrangement' maps to the Fibonacci-pair parastichy counts (clockwise and anticlockwise spiral numbers). No modern reinterpretation beyond treating the larger of the two counts as the ordinal index of the pair. The Dryad landing page does not describe columns, so the diameter field in the anonymised public-submission spreadsheet is unconfirmed and must be checked on download. Parastichy counts come from the author's count-data spreadsheet, linked to heads by ID.

dataset.name: Data from: Novel Fibonacci and non-Fibonacci structure in the sunflower: results of a citizen science experiment
dataset.publisher: Dryad (data by Swinton and Ochu, Royal Society Open Science 2016)
dataset.why_it_fits: Public data on about 657 sunflower seedheads with parastichy counts (MSF007_Countdata and MSF007_SunflowerData_anonymised spreadsheets) plus annotated images, so the count-to-size relationship can be tested. Head diameter is expected in the public-submission spreadsheet but the landing page does not list columns, so this is unconfirmed. If absent, diameter could be measured from the annotated images.
